#84697. Industry News: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3271 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3271 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources.
  • It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.
  • “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

According to recent reports, “I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”.

According to recent reports, what a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Recent findings suggest that another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

According to recent reports, to say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

Industry observers note that the Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton mentioned after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It has been revealed that it could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”.

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”.

It has been revealed that gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My initiative is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

Industry observers note that he told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”.

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”.

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen stated to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

According to recent reports, “We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”.

Here’s what he remarked immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”.

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY.

It has been revealed that he notes: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”.

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

In a recent development, alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Piastri may be in for some bother.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql.

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs.

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

According to recent reports, alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu.

Industry observers note that pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Sources indicate that monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2.

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I mentioned earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC.

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”.

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M.

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6.

I’m as significant a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car manufacturer, isn’t there?

Sources indicate that 🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx.

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI.

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

It has been revealed that “Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’.

According to recent reports, “Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”.

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

According to recent reports, schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a substantial moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft.

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

The pair are just natural friends.

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton stated yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”.

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

It has been revealed that hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

According to recent reports, “It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”.

It has been revealed that russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

Sources indicate that however, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bech vede nel difensore un possibile punto fermo della Danimarca e considera aperto il futuro contrattuale dell’esterno.

Industry observers note that gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard stanno vivendo un momento di forma che, secondo il giornalista danese Malthe Bech di Bold, ha dato a entrambi un ruolo importante nella nazionale. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, I due giocatori della Lazio sono anche al centro dell’attenzione sul mercato italiano e internazionale. Bech ha parlato del loro rendimento, della squadra di Gennaro Gattuso e del percorso che li ha portati fin qui.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that bech non si aspettava di trovare la Lazio al primo posto in Serie A a questo punto del campionato. Immaginava che i biancocelesti potessero competere per un piazzamento tra le prime cinque, ma non un avvio così positivo: «Sono molto sorpreso da quanto bene abbia iniziato la stagione la Lazio. Mi aspettavo che lottasse per un posto tra le prime cinque, ma certamente non avrei immaginato di vederla in testa alla classifica della Serie A a questo punto del campionato».

Recent findings suggest that il giornalista considera Isaksen e Provstgaard tra i danesi più in forma della stagione. Entrambi, racconta, hanno ricevuto apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico Brian Riemer e occupano posizioni di rilievo nella nazionale: «Gustav Isaksen e Oliver Provstgaard sono due dei calciatori danesi che stanno attraversando il miglior momento di forma in questa stagione. Entrambi hanno ricevuto numerosi apprezzamenti dal commissario tecnico della Danimarca, Brian Riemer, e ricoprono anche ruoli molto importanti nella nazionale.».

In nazionale Isaksen è un riferimento per l’attacco, soprattutto sulla destra. Bech descrive così il suo coinvolgimento nel gioco danese: «Isaksen è uno dei principali riferimenti offensivi della Danimarca: gran parte della manovra d'attacco della squadra passa dai suoi piedi, soprattutto sulla fascia destra.».

L’esterno ha iniziato la stagione in modo convincente. Per Bech, se manterrà questo rendimento, potrà disputare la migliore annata della sua carriera. Il giornalista indica finora come suo riferimento la stagione 2022/23, chiusa da capocannoniere della Superliga danese. In quell’annata Isaksen segnò anche due gol contro la Lazio: Bech ritiene probabile che il club biancoceleste abbia cominciato allora a interessarsi a lui.

Sul contratto, Bech ritiene che il giocatore sarebbe disponibile a prolungare l’accordo con la Lazio, ma lascia aperte le possibilità: alla scadenza mancano meno di due anni. A suo giudizio Isaksen sembra felice a Roma e a proprio agio in Italia, come il calciatore stesso ha dichiarato in più occasioni.

Grandissima prestazione da parte dei ragazzi di Vecchi, che giocano a viso aperto contro la dominatrice del girone C di Serie C e conquistano un altro successo prestigioso, confermando la propria fama di "ammazza major" (dopo i trionfi contro Catania, Foggia, Crotone e Salernitana). I nerazzurri di Vecchi passano in vantaggio al 16' con un gran gol di Marello, ma pochi minuti dopo Selleri trova il pareggio. Nella ripresa gli ospiti hanno la chance di ribaltare il risultato con un calcio di rigore assegnato per fallo di mano di Fiordilino su tiro di Petrungaro, ma Melgrati para il tentativo dal dischetto di Castorani. Nel finale l'Inter trova la giocata decisiva con Agbonifo, che si inventa un sinistro dalla distanza e fa esplodere la panchina nerazzurra.

(ANSA) - MILANO, 21 NOV - "Sono state belle giornate, ho avuto un paio di giornate di incontri molto positivi a Casa Milan, in vista del mercato di gennaio e per tutti i piani per il resto della stagione. C'è un bel clima, oggi ottimo allenamento. La squadra sta bene, ho parlato con diversi giocatori e hanno tutti sensazioni positive e capiscono mister Amorim che sottolinea quanto sia importante la partita di domani. Speriamo di vincere e di continuare in modo positivo": lo dice il proprietario del Milan Gerry Cardinale prima di lasciare il centro sportivo rossonero dove ha seguito rifinitura e conferenza stampa alla vigilia della sfida contro il Frosinone.

Tra alcune notizie di mercato, Cardinale conferma che il rinnovo di Rabiot è vicino: "Amo Adrien, è uno dei miei giocatori preferiti. È fantastico. Ho enorme rispetto per lui e la sua famiglia. Stiamo parlando e spero di arrivare presto ad un lieto fine. Penso che debba essere un giocatore simbolo del Milan". (ANSA).

Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4382 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • Industry observers note that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Industry observers note that even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Sources indicate that ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

In a recent development, “It indicates where we have potential,” he mentioned. “There are elements to improve offensively.

In a recent development, “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads demonstrated substantial character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

In a recent development, A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

It has been revealed that in truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a newly introduced manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

It has been revealed that when Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another newly introduced signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

Sources indicate that that is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss noted: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

It has been revealed that “We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads indicated the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV.

"Since the newly introduced manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE.

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

It has been revealed that dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

In a recent development, the noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

In a recent development, bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

In a recent development, murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

In a recent development, scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

According to recent reports, the current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

In a recent development, safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Industry observers note that newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

In a recent development, the pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

In a recent development, jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls latest signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

In a recent development, it looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

According to recent reports, newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

According to recent reports, wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

Newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

It has been revealed that despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

According to recent reports, at opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 18:36 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:37 EST, 16 November 2026.

Max Dowman broke another record as the 16-year-old became the youngest-ever goalscorer for England's Under-21 side on Monday night.

The Arsenal teenager has already broken a plethora of records at club level, and is now taking that to the international stage too, breaking a record set by senior team star Jude Bellingham, who scored aged 17 years and 67 days in 2020.

Dowman was called into the U21 squad for the first time this international break, and made his debut off the bench in the 1-0 defeat by Portugal on Friday.

On Monday, meanwhile, he was given a start by manager Lee Carsley, and rewarded his manager's faith with an 89th-minute winner to break the record and earn his side a 3-2 win.

It's a record he can add to his already-extensive collection, which includes being the youngest Champions League player, the youngest Premier League goalscorer, and the youngest Premier League winner.

Manager Lee Carsley mentioned after the game: 'He played really well - he was one of four or five outstanding performances. Mikey Moore, Max, Ethan (Nwaneri), they were very good.

Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goal scorer when he scored against France on Monday.

'We see how good on the ball he is but he was outstanding off the ball. You have to keep reminding yourself about his age. There's a lot of expectation around him and he seems to handle that so well.

According to recent reports, 'It's notable we keep supporting him and he develops at his own pace. It's so important he enjoys his football.

'Obviously all the players in the squad are under pressure from their clubs and the expectation that surrounds them, so as much as we can we have to make that as easy as we can.'.

Despite bursting onto the scene last season, Dowman has just 19 minutes to his name in the top flight this campaign as Arsenal look to defend their title.

He has played a number of games for the Gunners' U21 side, while he was sent off against League Two side Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup.

Arteta scolded his player at the time, but remarked: 'I haven't seen the reaction to my reaction. Whether that's positive or negative. You need to understand the context, the relationship I have with him and what we discussed before we went out.

'If you see the reaction from my mother and father with me sometimes, you'd say "you don't like that reaction", but for me it was the best reaction ever as it enabled me to be who I am.

The Arsenal teenager, 16, broke the record held by Jude Bellingham with his late winner.

'But you want to see the best and most beautiful reaction. You want to see the reaction of his team-mates when they have to play with 10 men.

In a recent development, 'What do you expect? That's the level and that's the reaction. Whether it's right or wrong, that's the reaction. And the reaction when I don't win, I'm f****d off, big time.

It has been revealed that 'This is the environment and the reality. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League. We look after him so much but we are also demanding as he needs to earn the right to play otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me?'.

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Stefano Vecchi, tecnico dell'Inter U23, ha parlato in sala stampa dopo il successo contro il Potenza: "Oggi per vincere abbiamo avuto bisogno di tutti. Questa è la vittoria del gruppo, di tutti: del portiere che ha fatto parate importanti, degli attaccanti, di chi è entrato e ha risolto la partita come Agbonifo. Come ho sempre detto è un gruppo di ragazzi che lavora sodo e bene, si fanno sempre trovare pronti, e contro un Potenza di questo tipo ce n'era bisogno. Quando si gioca tutti al massimo delle potenzialità, quest'anno siamo competitivi e stiamo bene in campo con tutti. Poi è anche vero che nel secondo tempo il Potenza ci ha messo grande pressione. Siamo stati bravi anche a soffrire, cosa non scontata per una squadra della nostra età".

Si può dire che quest'anno la squadra ha compiuto il passo in avanti dal punto di vista della maturità?

"Siamo cresciuti tutti, in un girone molto impegnativo e complicato come il C. Ci rendiamo conto di essere competitivi con tutti: l'anno scorso c'erano partite che per mezz'ora o dei tempi sembrava di essere in balia dell'avversario e di prendere delle imbarcate clamorose. Quest'anno invece no, un po' perchè la qualità dei ragazzi è alta, un po' perchè chi è rimasto ha un'esperienza diversa".

A inizio stagione forse una vittoria del genere non sarebbe arrivata: cosa è cambiato?

Sources indicate that "Cambiato non lo so, sicuramente siamo una squadra che deve lavorare per migliorare. I ragazzi sono molto giovani, ma al tempo stesso non darei per scontata questa cosa: dobbiamo tenere i piedi per terra e continuare a lavorare sodo. Tanti dei nostri sono all'inizio della nostra carriera, non possono accontentarsi di una partita fatta bena all'interno di un campionato o di essere come adesso se vogliono giocare in Serie A, come giustamente ambiscono i nostri ragazzi".

Quanto aiutano partite come queste a crescere?

In a recent development, "Sicuramente aiuta, a patto che si riesca a rimanere con i piedi per terra e non ci si senta arrivati dopo aver battuto la prima. La classifica parla chiaro, il Potenza non ha quei punti per caso e l'ha dimostrato anche oggi nel secondo tempo. Noi siamo stati in partita, quando ci siamo tutti e giochiamo da squadra possiamo vincere".

Charlys e Kaczmarski hanno disputato una buona gara.

It has been revealed that "Sono ragazzi con potenzialità importanti, sono i nostri giovani "più vecchi" essendo dei 2004, hanno già avuto esperienza e stanno dimostrando di essere pronti per un salto importante. Se sono qua è perchè prima non hanno dimostrato queste potenzialità, adesso le stanno tirando fuori e anche loro devono usare questa squadra come un trampolino di lancio, ma lo fai se la squadra raggiunge risultati: prima il gruppo e poi singolarmente arriveranno soddisfazioni".

Il Potenza ha la possibilità di rimanere al vertice?

Industry observers note that "Ho visto un Potenza che ha provato vincere, consapevole della propria forza, e nel secondo tempo siamo stati un po' in affanno. Poi siamo stati bravi a portarla dalla nostra parte con la bravura di Melgrati e anche per quello che abbiamo creato. Il Potenza ha dimostrato di essere meritatamente là davanti, poi se riuscirà a rimanere là dipende dalla sua bravura e magari da qualche passo falso di qualche squadra importante. Ho vinto un campionato con la Feralpi Salò, è possibile tutto nel calcio, anche che qualche realtà che parte dietro possa superare le favorite".

Si aspettava un Potenza arrembante? Avevate preparato la partita così?

It has been revealed that "Il Potenza ha grandissima qualità, giocatori che sanno ribaltare l'azione con grande gamba e velocità. Sapevamo di questa loro qualità, ma non sempre si riesce a fare quello che si vorrebbe. Nel secondo tempo siamo costretti ad abbassarci perchè il Potenza ha spinto. Spesso gli episodi indirizzano la gara, oggi sono stati dalla nostra parte. credo comunque che la vittoria sia stata meritata. Abbiamo un portiere e lo paghiamo per parare! E poi, nella fatica, i miai ragazzo non hanno mai mollato: ci portiamo a casa anche quella convinzione di averla meritata".

Come mai c'è stata un'Inter diversa tra primo e secondo tempo?

According to recent reports, "Merito del Potenza. Noi siamo calati fisicamente con qualche ragazzo. Abbiamo avuto una settimana di stop, qualche ragazzo è andato via con le Nazionali, qualcuno è stato in Prima Squadra, qualcuno ha giocato tre partite in una settimana in Nazionale e altri che non hanno proprio giocato. Quelli che si sono allenati con noi erano in 7-8: quando c'è la sosta per le Nazionali per noi è un problema preparare fisicamente la squadra. Oggi abbiamo sofferto la veemenza del Potenza, forse avrei potuto fare qualche cambio prima per dare più freschezza".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Risultato finale: Napoli-Torino 1-0.

Industry observers note that il Napoli crea tanto, spreca, rischia, ma alla fine la porta a casa: contro il Torino la decide il solito Scott McTominay con un gol nella ripresa su invito di Noa Lang. Lo scozzese è dominante ed è suo il voto più alto di questa sfida dello stadio Maradona. Ecco di seguito le pagelle a cura della redazione di TuttoMercatoWeb.com.

LE PAGELLE DEL NAPOLI (di Daniele Najjar).

Milinkovic-Savic 6,5 - Attento su Gineitis, risponde presente anche sulla punizione insidiosa di Mandragora. Nel finale i palloni alti sono tutti suoi.

Beukema 6 - Qualche fastidio Cacciamani glielo crea nel corso dei 90 minuti, ma nel complesso regge l'urto e concede il giusto.

In a recent development, rrahmani 6,5 - Simeone è un cliente impegnativo e che i suoi compiti di difesa del pallone li svolge bene. Rrahmani però in area gli concede poco e mette l'elmetto negli ultimi venti minuti.

Marin 5,5- Primo tempo in cui non corre rischi, ma sembra a tratti insicuro e quando pasticcia su Simeone rischia di far segnare il Torino. Allegri lo cambia poco dopo. (Dal 58' Olivera 6 - Entra e porta spinta e attenzione: la solita affidabilità su quella fascia).

Sources indicate that politano 6,5 - Invito a De Bruyne, va vicino al gol per due volte e porta diversi cross interessanti. Niente di trascendentale, ma il suo apporto si sente ed esce stremato (dall'82' Favasuli s.v.).

Anguissa 6,5 - Non sembra ancora il vero Anguissa, quello dominante del periodo con Conte, ma certamente il possesso in mediana del Napoli è vasto anche grazie alla sua presenza e si sacrifica tanto per la squadra.

Gilmour 6,5 - Prezioso per come rattoppa nelle occasioni in cui il Torino prova a ripartire, così spende un giallo per fermare una potenziale occasione.

McTominay 8 - A tratti sembra Bud Spencer nel film "Lo chamavano Bulldozer": uno contro tutti. In settimana ha spiegato come Conte gli abbia insegnato a trasformarsi da gregario a giocatore dominante: può mandargli un altro messaggio per ringraziare. Fa di tutto per segnare, alla fine la spedisce all'angolino con un missile dei suoi.

Industry observers note that spinazzola 6 - Buon rientro il suo: non aveva i 90 minuti, ma in un'ora copre e spinge. (Dal 58' Lang 6,5 - Accolto dai fischi del Maradona, la prima giocata è un cross in curva. Reagisce: diagonale da terzino su Aboukhlal, palla recuperata e data a McTominay per l'1-0. Segnale?).

Vergara s.v. - Si ferma dopo soli 11 minuti: che sfortuna (dal 12' De Bruyne 6,5- Altro che stanco: gioca con il piglio di chi ha qualcosa da far vedere ed è subito ben presente in ogni azione offensiva dei suoi).

Sources indicate that hojlund 6,5 - Frustata sulla quale Perri si esalta, di testa manda alto. È ben presente e fa sudare sette camicie ai difensori: va sempre in guerra. (Dall'82' Giovane s.v.).

Allenatore: Massimiliano Allegri 6,5 - Rosa ridotta al minimo dagli infortuni e si ferma ancora Vergara. Un mese dopo però arriva di nuovo una vittoria. Resta l'impressione che a questa squadra manchi sempre qualcosina per essere a posto, ma i tre punti di oggi sono fondamentali per provare a svoltare. E per respirare.

LE PAGELLE DEL TORINO (di Marco Pieracci).

Perri 7 - Reattivo nel dire subito di no a Politano, si esalta sul tiro al bersaglio del Napoli: sfiora la doppia cifra di parate, alcune sono da portiere top. Cede solo in extremis.

Coco 6 - Deve preoccuparsi degli inserimenti a rimorchio di McTominay, se lo fa sfuggire in qualche situazione ma alla fine non paga dazio. Mura il colpo di testa in tuffo di De Bruyne.

It has been revealed that ismajli 6,5 - Affronta Hojlund a petto in fuori, raramente gli concede la possibilità di attaccare la profondità alle sue spalle: risolutivo in almeno tre occasioni con interventi in scivolata. Dal 72’ Comert 5,5 - Entra e nel giro di una manciata di secondi il muro difensivo granata crolla, con l'uscita di Ismajli il reparto perde una certezza granitica.

Comuzzo 5,5 - In affanno sulle folate offensive degli attaccanti azzurri, è il più in difficoltà dietro. Si propone spesso in sovrapposizione, per aggiungere una soluzione in più.

Belghali 6 - Recuperato in extremis, è meno arrembante del solito forse perché non guarito del tutto: il ginocchio gli presenta il conto, costringendolo al cambio per la classica ricaduta. Dal 40’ Aboukhlal 5 - Vicino al gol in contropiede, non angola abbastanza la conclusione in diagonale. Mangiato da Lang nell’episodio decisivo.

It has been revealed that bragança 5,5 - Preciso nella distribuzione del pallone, anche se lo fa giocando quasi esclusivamente per vie orizzontali e in maniera troppo prudente. così rallenta troppo l’azione. Dal 46’ Vlasic 6 - Pianta le tende sulla trequarti, alza il livello di pericolosità.

In a recent development, mandragora 6,5 - Fulcro della mediana, assicura la protezione necessaria alla difesa. Capacità balistiche fuori dal comune, colpisce una traversa clamorosa. Pericoloso anche da fermo.

Gineitis 6 - Titolare scelto per arginare la fisicità di Anguissa, non si risparmia nei duelli ingaggiati tenendo il passo degli avversari. Lucida il sinistro, senza lasciare il segno. Dal 67’ Casadei 5,5 - Involuto, non emerge.

Cacciamani 6,5 - Zero timori nel puntare Politano, è molto coinvolto fin dalle prime battute: di gran lunga il più intraprendente in avvio, gli manca il guizzo finale però non perde intensità.

Sources indicate that adams 6 - Di palloni giocabili in area ne transitano pochini, così arretra il raggio d’azione per cercarseli. Partita di lotta più che di governo, dà una mano come rifinitore con generosità.

In a recent development, simeone 5,5 - Partita amarcord, di solito non è tipo che fa sconti ma stavolta fa un’eccezione: soffre le attenzioni di Rrahmani e Beukema, si consola con gli applausi del Maradona. Dal 72’ Zapata 5,5 - Di possibilità per far male nel finale di partita ce ne sarebbero, non le capitalizza.

Allenatore: Abate 6 - Toro bello compatto, organizzato con le distanze corrette fra i reparti e pronto a sfruttare le debolezze di un Napoli convalescente. Tutto bene fino agli ultimi sedici metri, dove servirebbe maggior imprevedibilità. Resta la buona prestazione, ma anche tanto da migliorare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, il Napoli Primavera non va oltre l’1 a 1 casalingo contro il Perugia. Al termine del match ha parlato il tecnico della Primavera Antonio Nocerino, ecco le sue dichiarazioni:.

Recent findings suggest that “Abbiamo fatto una buona gara, ma ci sono cose che a me non piacciono. Mi aspetto pochi errori e che non si sbaglia dalla gente tecnica, troppi errori nell’ultimo passaggio. La prestazione è buona, i ragazzi sono stati bravissimo, noi ieri l’abbiamo preparata che tanti erano in prima squadra. Abbiamo giocato contro una squadra che ha i punti che merita e gioca molto bene. Se andiamo a vedere la partita sono rammaricato, mi sono intristito, hai tante opportunità e non chiudi la partita, poi vabbè il rigore..sono cose che ci possono stare”.

According to recent reports, sulla fase difensiva: “Andando spesso uomo contro uomo, noi lavoriamo tanto sul doppio lavoro, cercando di mettersi a 1 metro e mezzo dalla distanza, sia per coprire palla nello spazio che essere pronti ad attaccare. Marotta? Al di là dell’espulsione è un giocatore molto importante per noi, dovrebbe essere più lucido nelle situazione di gara, ma questo fa parte della crescita e migliorare nella frenata e non andare di intuito, per portarlo dove vuoi tu. Ogni tanto capita l’errore, fa parte del percorso di questa stagione”.

Sources indicate that su Spinelli e Pereyra in prima squadra: “Sono contento e orgoglioso, vuol dire che il lavoro stanno facendo è giusto. Ma questo non basta, non bisogna accontentarsi, fare sempre qualche cosa in più; andare in prima squadra è bellissimo, poi bisogna farsi trovare pronto per stare più tempo e magari entrare, nel calcio non si può mai sapere”.

Sources indicate that sulla Youth League: “Non siamo ancora come io vorrei, a volte devi accompagnare i ragazzi, che ancora non hanno vissuto il calcio dei grandi, piano piano stiamo cercando di fargli capire che devono essere pronti sempre. Sono bravi ragazzi e avere una mentalità forte li metterà in condizione di affrontare prime squadre. L’obiettivo è dargli autostima e meno negatività, cercando di aiutarli in questo percorso, non lasciarli abbattere. Le cose negative vengono, ma l’importante è reagire e quello è l’obiettivo che noi cerchiamo a livello emotivo”.

Sources indicate that sul Centro Sportivo: “Sicuramente deve alimentare l’entusiasmo, ormai sono tanti anni che vivo fuori e ho visto un pò tutto. A me dispiace è che si deve andare a vedere il negativo, quella cosa che non è costruttiva. Se io ho la possibilità e ho un presidente che cerca di fare qualcosa, io devo essere solo orgoglioso e onorato da napoletano, in modo che i napoletani non debbano andare via e possano avere la fortuna di essere in campi dove prepararsi fisicamente e mentalmente. Ormai quando uno fa c’è sempre qualcosa da dire, per Napoli è qualcosa che fa la differenza. Lo spero soprattutto per i ragazzi e per fargli coltivare il proprio talento. La cosa che mi sta deludendo è la negatività, non si guarda mai a chi vuole fare qualcosa di diverso che crede nella città. Chi non fa alla fine parla, deve solo parlare e buttare via l’aria alla bocca, io preferisco chi fa e alla fine sarà sempre criticato. Si tratta della mentalità italiana, c’è gelosia e invidia di chi vuole successo. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 17:56 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 19:19 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.
  • The 23-year-old has had a tough time of it at Anfield since his £116million move to the club last summer, but has never really struggled on the international stage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 17:56 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 19:19 EST, 16 November 2026.

Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz scored a stunning brace for Germany as Jurgen Klopp's side thumped the Netherlands in the Nations League.

The 23-year-old has had a tough time of it at Anfield since his £116million move to the club last summer, but has never really struggled on the international stage.

And he continued that trend on Monday evening with two goals for his side to help them top their Nations League group.

Sources indicate that his first was the pick of the bunch. Wirtz moved along the forward line as a Dutch side without Virgil van Dijk struggled to contain him. He picked up the ball around 25 yards out, cut inside onto his weaker left foot, and curled a pearling effort into the far corner off the post.

That goal, which came on the hour mark, put his side 2-0 up after Freiburg's Derry Scherhant had scored the opener, and Wirtz wasn't done there.

Centre back Nico Schlotterbeck made it 3-0 before the Liverpool man picked up his second of the night after drifting into the penalty box unmarked and finishing high after good work from Brajan Gruda.

According to recent reports, cette version de Wirtz avec le maillot de la Mannschaft c’est celle qu’on aimerait voir chaque semaine en PL. Quel missile pour faire le break ! Meilleur buteur allemand sur cette édition de l’UNL. 🇩🇪🔥 pic.twitter.com/m0DqaOungS.

Florian Wirtz scored a brace for Germany as they thumped the Netherlands 5-0 in Nations League action.

Liverpool midfielder Wirtz received a big hug from a smiling Jurgen Klopp at full time.

Gruda himself, who is on loan at RB Leipzig from Brighton, wrapped up the five-star win on a night that arguably saw Klopp announce himself as Germany boss.

After full-time, the ex-Liverpool manager gave Wirtz a huge hug as the duo beamed with big smiles on their faces.

While it was a night to remember for Germany, a Netherlands team that included the likes of Micky van de Ven, Jurrien Timber and Wirtz's Liverpool team-mate Cody Gakpo were left exasperated.

Van Dijk had pulled out of the squad with a knock after playing with a knock in recent weeks.

His side will still, though, compete in the Nations League quarter-finals after finishing second in the group, finishing ahead of Greece on goal difference.

As for Wirtz, he will hope his performance will help continue what has been an uphill climb so far this season.

He also found the net for Germany in their first match of the international break – a 3-1 win over Serbia – and picked up a goal and assist in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

In total, he has two goals and five assists in 15 games for Liverpool this season – though the Reds will hope those numbers increase as the season goes on.

His second goal came as he drifted into the penalty area and finished high into the net.

Last month, meanwhile, Reds manager Andoni Iraola insisted he has full faith in his midfielder.

It has been revealed that 'I think he has had a little bit of everything this season,' he stated. 'He has had good games, probably the other day was not his best game, especially offensively. We trust Florian.

It has been revealed that 'Florian is a very good player. He was coming from good performances in the international break, I think. I think it is a matter of everyone to find his moment.'.

Klopp hailed him 'exceptional', meanwhile, during the last international break.

Man United's first woman on their backroom team, the fitness enforcer, a scorpion-kicking goalkeeper coach... and his son! Meet Mauricio Pochettino's team of experts flying in to whip United's flops into shape

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.
  • The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.

The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone. With him, Pochettino brings to Old Trafford an experienced and familiar cast of trusted colleagues, who will be tasked with supporting him in his mission to turn things around in Manchester.

From a first-team coach who has known him since 1992 to the boss' own son, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the backroom staff accompanying Pochettino at United...

According to recent reports, when the Manchester United reporters turn up for press conferences at Carrington, they will notice one seat, usually in the front row and to the far left, has a reserved sign on it. It will be for Perez, who is Pochettino’s eyes and ears. Those same correspondents may well be followed by Perez on social media, so he can stay in the loop of what is being written.

Industry observers note that wherever Pochettino goes, so too does his shadow Perez. You have probably already heard about the time Pochettino met his idol Sir Alex Ferguson for lunch in London back in 2016. What you may not know is that Perez was there, too. He and Pochettino have been joined at the hip ever since they met in Barcelona when one was an analyst and the other was managing Espanyol.

Mauricio Pochettino (right) arrives at Manchester United with a trusted team of backroom staff.

That was in 2010. Perez had studied sports science at university and completed his coaching qualifications but was considering quitting football. Pochettino convinced him otherwise, and they soon learned they shared the same principles, including the importance of creating the right culture of togetherness within a club to succeed.

Industry observers note that in 2013, it was Perez’s turn to convince Pochettino. The Argentinian was unsure about moving to England to manage Southampton, but the Spaniard had spent a month on these shores studying how Premier League sides train and play.

He told Pochettino that the intensity of his sessions and style would fit perfectly and that he could not turn down the chance to take on the Premier League.

Sources indicate that they now consider each other family, and Perez’s story itself is a nice one. By his own admission, he will tell you he failed at becoming a professional player, but he believes the way in which he worked his way in as a coach can inspire others who dream of finding their own place in football.

It has been revealed that he loves the game, so much so that he would use days off to travel from London to Manchester to visit the National Football Museum. Now he will be living much closer to his favourite hotspot.

As well as being the glue which connects various club departments together, Perez is a fitness and conditioning specialist, and a normal working day might involve him arriving at the training ground at 7.30am.

After meeting with Pochettino over breakfast, he will then hold a 9am medical meeting where plans for each player are discussed and decided. Programmes tend to be tailored to individuals rather than set for the whole squad. Perez was credited with helping to establish Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur as among the fittest teams in the Premier League.

Where Pochettino is larger than life, Perez is unassuming, and has never sought to step into management as he prefers to work in the shadows.

Jesus Perez, pictured with Pochettino at Spurs in 2019, has long been his right-hand man.

We talk about Pochettino’s man-management prowess, but the same is true of Perez.

For example, when Chelsea beat Leicester City 4-2 in an FA Cup quarter-final in 2023-24, Raheem Sterling had a stinker. He missed a penalty, spurned a one-on-one and skied a free-kick. Chelsea’s fans booed him, and chanted ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ at Pochettino when he substituted Mykhailo Mudryk rather than Sterling after 78 minutes at 2-2. Perez was the first to go straight to Sterling to put an arm around him that day.

And when Cole Palmer was becoming a household name in Pochettino’s one and only season at Chelsea, Perez was among those who privately tried to help the Englishman understand the perils of the distractions of his new-found fame.

It has been revealed that when they departed Chelsea, Pochettino and Perez were men of their word and honoured their commitment to manage the World XI in the Soccer Aid charity match a few weeks later. That was despite the awkwardness of the game being held at Stamford Bridge. They lost 6-3 to Frank Lampard’s England XI.

MIGUEL D’AGOSTINO, FIRST-TEAM COACH.

To give a sense of how long Pochettino has known ‘Miki’, around 1992, Pochettino purchased his first car while a player for Newell’s Old Boys. He gave his team-mate a lift home. When D’Agostino went to get out of the car, the wind caught it hard, and broke Pochettino’s door. D'Agostino never paid the bill to have it fixed – something Pochettino occasionally likes to remind him of.

Miguel D'Agostino, known as 'Miki', has heaps of experience as a former analyst and scout.

The first-team coach has known Pochettino since 1992 (both pictured at Tottenham in 2019).

Pochettino clearly forgave his fellow defender, who was also plying his trade under Marcelo Bielsa.

Industry observers note that D’Agostino was an analyst at Espanyol, initially attached to the scouting department before assuming responsibility for filming training sessions and overseeing player analysis. From there, he followed Pochettino wherever he went, from Southampton to Tottenham to Paris Saint-Germain to Chelsea to the United States national team.

Recent findings suggest that while with the USA, D’Agostino would watch games in the MLS, going to Real Salt Lake or wherever there were players for scouting. In training, he is hands-on, sometimes with a stopwatch in hand or notepad containing that day’s drills.

Recent findings suggest that when Pochettino tested positive for Covid-19 in January 2021, D’Agostino and Perez took temporary charge of his PSG side. They beat Angers 1-0 away from home in Ligue 1.

All of Pochettino’s confidants have a good grasp of English.

SILVIA TUYA, STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING COACH.

The newest member of Pochettino’s inner circle, having joined his USA national set-up in October 2024.

With a PhD in sports science, Tuya had worked with FC Levante Badalona in Liga F, Spain’s top tier for women’s football, while she also served as a lecturer at the National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia at the University of Barcelona.

Since teaming up with Pochettino, she was seen on the training pitch and in the gym with the players.

Tuya will become Manchester United's first-ever female coach connected with the men's team.

Silvia Tuya is the newest member of Pochettino’s team, having joined his USA set-up in 2024.

Tuya is set to become Manchester United's first-ever female coach with the men's team.

TONI JIMENEZ, GOALKEEPING COACH.

After winning gold for Spain at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992, Jimenez met Pochettino in 1994 when they became team-mates for Espanyol, but it is worth recalling the 2000 Copa del Rey final when they found themselves on opposing sides.

The goalkeeper represented Atletico Madrid, and Pochettino was in defence for Espanyol, who won 2-1. After full-time, Pochettino delayed his celebrations to go and console his friend, who had already endured a challenging year with his father having passed away.

In a recent development, jimenez has never forgotten that kindness from Pochettino, and like the others, the two have worked together wherever the latter has managed, from Espanyol to Southampton to Tottenham to PSG to Chelsea to the USA. They have shared a fair few of their favourite mate teas in their time, and now for United, where Jimenez will work with Senne Lammens and Co.

Sources indicate that they say training is rarely boring when Jimenez is involved. He was happy to prove to Tottenham’s players during one tour of Malaysia that he could copy Rene Higuita’s scorpion kick save, for example, and is pretty good when testing his goalkeepers in free-kick practice. Lammens should beware he is liable to do a little dance if he scores past you, however.

Industry observers note that hugo Lloris, the former Spurs goalkeeper who won the 2018 World Cup with France, frequently credited the charismatic Jimenez for adding fresh areas to his game. Pochettino has also hailed Jimenez for how he keeps second and third-choice goalkeepers motivated when they are not playing.

Hugo Lloris frequently credited Toni Jimenez (pictured) for adding latest areas to his game.

Sebastiano Pochettino first worked with his father at Tottenham (pictured celebrating at PSG).

SEBASTIANO POCHETTINO, SPORTS SCIENTIST AND FITNESS COACH.

Industry observers note that the son of the manager. A graduate of Southampton Solent University, Sebastiano first worked with his father at Tottenham. It was stated that he had become the Premier League’s youngest sports scientist when he was hired at the age of 22.

He soon became a regular sight in training sessions and on match days, seen putting the players through their paces and with the substitutes as they warmed up.

Industry observers note that sebastiano became a fitness coach and joined his old man at PSG, Chelsea and the USA. One of his specialties is in injury prevention, and that includes monitoring the players’ sleep and mood.

Trust is important to Pochettino, and he knows he can rely on family.

Hired by the USA as their men's national team lead analyst in August 2023 - just over a year before Pochettino took charge - Scott previously spent eight years at the FA before moving to Inter Miami.

He graduated from Liverpool John Moores University, achieving a first class BsC in Science and Football, with his major project titled 'A Comparison of the Technical Demands in Academy and Reserve Team Soccer'.

He went on to complete a PhD in Exercise Psychology & Performance Analysis there, before putting his skills to use during internships at Everton and Liverpool before joining the FA.

Scott has clearly impressed Pochettino, who confirmed before Tuesday's clash with Haiti that he was among those staying with him for that game before joining United - with Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr having travelled to England already.

'I am with Miguel and Silvia and Alec [for this game],' he said. 'After, they are going to join me in Manchester.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

In a recent development, the substantial moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

It has been revealed that on this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams remarked: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

It has been revealed that glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

According to recent reports, the grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

In a recent development, one of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

It has been revealed that after the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1.

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

It has been revealed that brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘upcoming’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

It has been revealed that iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Industry observers note that enzo jeered by Coventry fans when taken off was predictable. Replaced by Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

And Mykhailo Mudryk is on for his first appearance since November 2024.

In a recent development, forest are feeling aggrieved over that disallowed goal. Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot.

Big cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that that is a substantial chance for Coventry. Loum Tchaouna got room in the penalty area and it needed Gianluigi Donnarumma to save low to his right.

Luka Vuskovic heads in from an inswinging corner.

Controversy at the City Ground – and it’s again a result of Var.

Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Neco Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goalline.

Sources indicate that the goal did go to Var for a possible handball by Williams, and it was ruled that the Wales international did handle it. Did look very harsh.

So it remains 0-0 at the City Ground.

Sources indicate that coventry are still in this game but City have their chances to put them away. Enzo was deemed offside when he set up a strike for Haaland. The UK’s most expensive player has got better during this game.

Looks like it will be ruled out for handball.

Vitaly Janelt breaks the deadlock after Brentford were battered in the first half.
