The massive headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

According to recent reports, “I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca mentioned, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more notable to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

Recent findings suggest that “Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

In a recent development, “I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

Industry observers note that “I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”.

According to recent reports, maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Sources indicate that good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

Recent findings suggest that we have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi aims to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

The Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health concerns, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

In a recent development, 'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

Industry observers note that 'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

In a recent development, 'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

According to recent reports, mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health issues at Birmingham City.

According to recent reports, the veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he stated. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

Recent findings suggest that speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he notes. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

Recent findings suggest that 'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

Mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health issue is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

Industry observers note that 'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

Recent findings suggest that 'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'.

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood said: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he reveals for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

In a recent development, 'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'.

Sources indicate that roma Capitale. Ci stiamo avviando a un derby incredibile. Un derby con vista scudetto. Il 13 dicembre ci sarà da divertirci. Dopo la sosta per la Nazionale, l'ultima di questo 2026, il campionato regala un sabato nel segno di Roma. Con due squadre che avevano iniziato la stagione con obiettivi diversi e che ora si ritrovano a duellare sullo stesso palcoscenico. Pochi mesi fa la Lazio era un'area terremotata. Rottura totale tra tifosi e il presidente Lotito, mercato bloccato da una crisi economica soffocante e per rendere la situazione ancora più bollente una clamorosa eliminazione al primo turno di Coppa Italia contro un'avversaria di categoria inferiore. Gattuso, il nuovo allenatore della squadra biancoceleste, poteva finire schiacciato da tutte queste criticità. Invece, probabilmente, proprio nel momento più delicato è nata una magia. Una di quelle che rendono il calcio speciale. Oggi, dopo aver battuto all'Olimpico il Lecce, la Lazio è in testa alla classifica. La squadra biancoceleste può vincere lo scudetto? Sì, può provarci. Non è la formazione più forte del campionato e, di sicuro, non è la favorita. Ma ci sono alcuni buoni motivi per immaginare la Lazio in corsa per il titolo: 1) Gattuso ha costruito un gruppo fantastico; 2) in rosa ci sono giocatori di qualità in ogni reparto; 3) Noslin cresce in maniera impressionante; 4) non fare le Coppe regala punti di vantaggio ai biancocelesti e 5) come ha detto un ex grande del calcio italiano come Sebino Nela (tra l'altro ha vinto uno scudetto con la Roma...) questa Lazio ricorda lo scudettato Verona di Bagnoli.

Anche la Roma può vincere il titolo. In questo caso non si può parlare di sorpresa. La squadra giallorossa era tra le favorite per lo scudetto fin dall'inizio del torneo. Contro il Parma è arrivata un'altra testimonianza della forza di questa Roma. Una macchina da gol. Anche per i giallorossi ci sono alcuni buoni motivi per vederla con il tricolore cucito sul petto: 1) Malen sembra il Batistuta protagonista dell'ultimo scudetto della Roma; 2) Gasperini è un fattore con il suo calcio e le sue idee; 3) Dybala e Soule, stavolta proposti a staffetta, sono una coppia micidiale; 4) la Roma nel 2027 festeggerà il Centenario un motivo in più per centrare un grande risultato e 5) la famiglia Friedkin è pronta a garantire altri due rinforzi nel mercato invernale.

È stato anche un grande sabato per il Como. Mister Fabregas è riuscito a voltare pagina dopo la batosta rimediata contro l'Inter prima dello stop e dopo le cattive notizie sulle condizioni fisiche di Kean. Un investimento da quaranta milioni che non ha dato frutti e non li darà per altri mesi. Il Como però ha trovato un suo equilibrio, sa gestire i momenti delle partite, sa andare oltre i momenti di difficoltà. E ha un giocatore speciale come Ramon capace di segnare un gol fondamentale e di evitarne uno con un incredibile recupero difensivo. Normale che sia nel mirino del Real Madrid. Ma intanto se lo gode il Como. E questo Como ha tutto per essere la mina vagante del campionato. Con tutte le carte in regola per riconquistare un posto nella prossima Champions.

It has been revealed that chiudiamo con il Napoli. La vittoria sul Torino allontana i problemi. Anche se la squadra di Allegri resta malaticcia. Un aspetto però emerge chiaro: De Laurentiis deve fare di tutto per allungare prima possibile il contratto a McTominay. È lui la figura intorno alla quale ricostruire un progetto vincente. Dopo aver risolto i suoi problemi di salute sta segnando a raffica. Se il Napoli è ancora vivo e se Allegri è ancora sulla panchina partenopea è tutto merito suo.

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Mattia Marello, esterno sinistro dell'Inter U23 e autore del primo gol nella vittoria contro il Potenza, ha parlato in conferenza stampa al termine del match: "Sono super contento per la squadra e per il mio gol perché ha contribuito alla vittoria. Sono molto contento della prestazione perché era una gara difficile, contro una squadra che arrivava da un periodo importante, che è a +9 sulla seconda".

Cosa scatta nella testa di ragazzi come te alla prima esperienza tra i professionisti quando si è chiamati ad affrontare squadre di categoria? Cosa vi viene chiesto?

It has been revealed that "Venivamo da una settimana difficile, io come tanti altri siamo stati in Nazionale, altri erano con la Prima Squadra, e quindi non siamo riusciti ad allenarci bene. Abbiamo preparato la partita in pochi giorni, ma sono stati molto importanti perché abbiamo fatto gruppo. Il mister ci ha parlato tanto prima e dopo l'allenamento, ci ha detto molto del Potenza insieme al suo staff e l'abbiamo preparata alla grande. Eravamo gasati".

Difficile preparare una gara con l'uscita di GTA?

Sources indicate that "GTA? Non ho la Play Station, non è un mio problema... Magari altri hanno sofferto questo momento, ma non è il mio caso! Sono molto contento per la partita, eravamo gasati anche prima, il mister ci ha fatto un bel discorso e ci ha preparati. Sapevamo che non sarebbe stata una partita come le altre".

In cosa puoi migliorare ancora?

In a recent development, "Parlo sempre tanto con il mister e i suoi collaboratori, lo chiedo anche io. Io cerco di migliorarmi ogni giorno su tutto, anche sulle cose in cui sono più forte, però principalmente cerco di allenare il piede debole e le letture difensive per diventare un calciatore completo".

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that nel basket, un tiro da fuori può valere tre punti.
  • Curiosamente, il gol che rende felice Allegri arriva pochi giorni dopo uno scambio di complimenti tra McTominay e Antonio Conte.
  • Il rapporto tra i due è rimasto ottimo anche dopo l'addio di Conte, ma adesso McTominay è soprattutto una risorsa fondamentale per Allegri.

Industry observers note that nel basket, un tiro da fuori può valere tre punti. Nel calcio un gol vale sempre uno, ma quello di Scott McTominay, che ha deciso Napoli-Torino 1-0, pesa di più. Perché consegna tre punti fondamentali alla formazione azzurra, ma soprattutto consente a Massimiliano Allegri di riprendere fiato dopo una sosta per le nazionali nella quale attorno alla sua panchina si era fatta parecchio pesante l'aria. Lo scozzese ha risolto una partita che il Napoli aveva a lungo controllato, senza riuscire a trovare la rete, e di cui era il migliore anche a prescindere dalla marcatura. Una vittoria che non cancella i problemi delle ultime settimane, ma permette al tecnico livornese di lavorare con maggiore serenità.

Curiosamente, il gol che rende felice Allegri arriva pochi giorni dopo uno scambio di complimenti tra McTominay e Antonio Conte. Lo scozzese ha raccontato quanto l'ex allenatore del Napoli sia stato importante nella sua evoluzione calcistica, soprattutto sul piano della mentalità. Non più un mediano chiamato semplicemente a svolgere determinati compiti, ma un giocatore consapevole di poter decidere le partite. Parole che Conte ha particolarmente apprezzato: "Quando leggi parole del genere, ti ripagano anche di alcune cose che possono averti dato fastidio". L'attuale tecnico del Bologna ha inoltre rivendicato il proprio ruolo nell'arrivo dell'ex Manchester United a Napoli, ricordando come la presenza di un allenatore vincente possa influenzare le scelte di mercato dei calciatori.

Il rapporto tra i due è rimasto ottimo anche dopo l'addio di Conte, ma adesso McTominay è soprattutto una risorsa fondamentale per Allegri. Il tecnico livornese gli chiede più lavoro di equilibrio in mezzo al campo, come ai tempi dello United, senza rinunciare alla sua capacità di inserirsi e trovare la porta. Anche perché non ha tantissime frecce nella sua faretra. Il gol al Torino conferma l'importanza dello scozzese, in una serata nella quale il Napoli aveva bisogno soprattutto di tornare a vincere, come ossigeno. Tre punti non bastano per risolvere tutto, ma cambiano almeno il clima. Più caldo di quello scozzese.

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

Industry observers note that the chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his fresh club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Sources indicate that morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

According to recent reports, instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In a recent development, in fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

In a recent development, all that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be noted that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Industry observers note that arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

Recent findings suggest that in the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

It has been revealed that A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

It has been revealed that chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

It has been revealed that ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

Industry observers note that “After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

Industry observers note that “It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher states Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

Sources indicate that “There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We revealed our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

In a recent development, “We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

According to recent reports, the final whistle is blown at the Emirates and Arsenal maintain their 100% record through three games as they have beaten Chelsea 2-1. They were 1-0 down inside the opening two minutes but goals from Havertz and Odegaard have led them to victory. Chelsea suffer their first competitive defeat under Xabi Alonso.

Pedro’s cross from the right has too much on it and Chavarria cannot head it back across goal. Chelsea’s last chance might have been that Estevao effort which was brilliantly saved by Raya.

Madueke is brought on late for Saka.

There will be four added minutes.

According to recent reports, that is a stunning save from Raya that may have preserved Arsenal’s victory. Estevao cuts in from the right and curls one towards the top corner. It looks set for the net but somehow Raya makes a fantastic save to deny Estevao.

According to recent reports, chelsea are bringing on Welbeck for Rogers, who is jeered by the Arsenal fans. Welbeck comes on with a note, that he gives to his captain James.

Arsenal have lost a bit of their composure and structure. I suspect that’s why Arteta has turned to Mikel Merino. He screamed at his bench immediately after a messy passage of play, and Merino emerged about 20 seconds later. Merino is very much the “sensible adult” sort of player, who should calm things down. Although he hasn’t yet.

Recent findings suggest that england team-mates Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers were really going at it there. Rogers absolutely furious with Rice tripping him up. “You should have signed for a significant club,” sing the Arsenal fans at Rogers...

In a recent development, it has kicked off. Rogers is cynically tripped by Rice but the referee somehow does not see it. Rogers is incensed and marches over to Rice, who has massively got away with one there. Rice knew exactly what he was doing as he deliberately trips Rogers. That is a nasty from Rice, who avoids a booking, yet Rogers is shown a yellow card. That is frankly dreadful refereeing.

Double change for Arsenal as Gyokeres and Merino come on for Havertz and Odegaard.

Gusto’s cross from the right is put behind by Konsa for a Chelsea corner out on the right. Neto clips it in but Arsenal head away. James then opts to shoot from range and his effort is blocked by Gabriel. That shot looked to be going on target but Raya may have had it covered anyway.

Sources indicate that rice’s corner from the left is flicked on by Havertz at the near post and the last touch comes off James for another Arsenal corner on the other side. Arsenal take it short and fell to get into the danger zone but do win themselves another corner.

Saka delivers it into a dangerous area and the ball is flicked, looking like it is going into the Chelsea net, but Martinez makes the save whilst on the ground.

Havertz plays a first-time flick into the path of Saka, whose first-time effort looking for the far corner is saved well by Martinez to his right.

Odegaard feeds a clever pass into the Chelsea penalty area to pick out Zubimendi, whose shot is blocked.

Double change for Arsenal as Zubimendi and Hincapie replace Lewis-Skelly and Calafiori.

Palmer gets a shot away from the right side of the box but it is straight at Raya. Chelsea are just starting to wrestle back some momentum.

Gusto has only just come on but has a chance. The ball is laid to him on the edge of the box and he hits it first time but his effort goes over the bar.

According to recent reports, the momentum is certainly with Arsenal right now so Xabi Alonso is making a double change. Gusto and Chavarria replace Lavia and Hato. With Gusto coming on for Lavia, Chelsea do not actually have any out-and-out central midfielders on the pitch.

Sources indicate that tzolis is the first Arsenal player into the book today. He is brought down by Lacroix and then demands that the Chelsea defender be booked, waving an imaginary card, and is then shown a yellow himself. Lacroix was also booked for the original foul.

Industry observers note that two former teammates challenge each other as Konsa slides in to make a perfectly-timed challenge on Rogers. The home crowd loved that tackle from Konsa, who won that tackle fair and square.

Chelsea made Odegaard angry about two minutes before that goal. The Arsenal captain, who is a mild-mannered guy, was really unhappy with a tackle by James. They were exchanging some verbals afterwards, before Odegaard then ran away from James to score.

That’s five goals Chelsea have conceded in just over a game-and-a-half since Emi Martinez took over in goal. In fairness, that Odegaard goal wasn’t his fault.

Arsenal were forced to respond when Chelsea scored early but now it is on the visitors to see how they respond after falling behind.

For the first time this afternoon, Arsenal lead and it is a quality goal. Tzolis receives it out on the left and cuts inside onto his right. He plays the ball inside towards Havertz, who is in space on the edge of the Chelsea box. It is really intelligent from Havertz, who dummies it to take away Fofana and allows the ball to run through to Odegaard, who takes one touch before firing past Martinez.

I think Chelsea are now 19 Premier League games without keeping a clean sheet, dating back to last season.

A few Chelsea players were having a moan at referee Christopher Kavanagh as they went off for half-time. But Alonso’s players need to calm down and keep their cool. There were signs the Blues’ old disciplinary problems could rear their head again with Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer being booked. Romeo Lavia also squared up to Ben White for no real reason. Chelsea have to keep 11 players on the pitch.

A really enjoyable half of football, even if it was slowed down a little in the last few minutes by a series of niggly fouls. Arsenal are the better team here but Chelsea are definitely dangerous. That Neto shot off the post was evidence of how rapidly they can hurt the Arsenal defence.

The first half is brought to an end and it is 1-1 going into the break at the Emirates.

Chelsea hit the post late on in the half. Chelsea counter from inside their own half and Pedro whips a ball first time down the right channel to pick out the run of Neto. The Portuguese forward drives at Gabriel inside the Arsenal box and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot. His effort comes back off the far post and Chelsea were inches away from retaking the lead.

That left side of the Arsenal defence again. Wide open for Neto to run into the space. Chelsea looking for the early ball every time.

Tensions are boiling over as Lavia and White come to blows. As Lavia shepherds the ball out of play, White threw himself to ground and wanted a free-kick. Lavia is not impressed by White’s antics and lets him know about it.

It has been revealed that is Palmer in some trouble? Raya catches a free-kick into his box and gets Arsenal going on the counter with a long ball forward. With Havertz getting away from him, Palmer brings him down and takes the yellow. There was another covering defender, hence why it was just a yellow.

There will be four added minutes.

As we approach half-time, there have been 15 shots in total from both sides in the game with nine of those being on target.

Chelsea win it just inside the Arsenal half after good defensive work from Lavia and Pedro then spots Raya off his line. The Chelsea forward therefore opts to shoot from a long way out but drags his effort wide.

According to recent reports, white and Havertz exchange a neat one-two down Arsenal’s right, with the latter clipping the ball to the back post. Lavia, with Saka right behind him, heads away well under pressure.

That is a decent opportunity for Rogers to get his second of the game. Pedro lays it off to him on the left side of the box and Rogers tries to curl one into the far corner but it goes wide.

Tremendous game at the Emirates. Both teams attacking one another. Chelsea have a lot of space with Pedro Neto on the right and keep using that diagonal ball. Once again, though, they look suspect in defence. The Havertz equaliser could have been stopped twice, but Chelsea defence just did not react. Fofana let Havertz past and Odegaard set a bit of a screen that stopped Lacroix getting close.

Former Chelsea player scores against former Arsenal goalkeeper. Interesting reaction from the Arsenal players to that Havertz goal: most of them ran straight back to their own half. They want to get on with this game. Suggests they can sense Chelsea’s vulnerability.

It is not always particularly significant when a manager says his player can be one of the best in the world. But it is probably worth taking notice when Xabi Alonso articulates his belief that Reece James can be one of the best midfielders on the planet.

For Liverpool, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Spain, Alonso was one of the finest midfielders of his generation and also played with some of the best midfielders in the world. So the Chelsea manager knows a thing or two about what it takes.

James has long been considered – when fit – one of the best right-backs in the world. But it had already been evident before the final 24 hours of the transfer window that the Chelsea player would spend a lot of time in midfield under Alonso.

Sources indicate that bukayo Saka has arrived at a career crossroads. We will soon learn whether he is destined to be a good Arsenal player or if he will elevate himself to the level of Premier League, Champions League and England great.

This weekend Saka turns 25, an age when footballers typically enter their peak. Although his legendary status at Arsenal is secure as a title winner, the reaction to the champions’ transfer window suggests there is a general feeling that he can and should produce more to earn “world class” status.

Mikel Arteta is short of such an attacker. He spent the summer investigating whether players of Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez’s calibre might add much-needed stardust to his front three. Failure to secure a big-name forward has led many to conclude that Arsenal’s title defence will be in the mould of their impressive, but cautious 1-0 victory at Aston Villa.

"It's another tough game"Ben White on coming up against Chelsea's front three 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/gfazGGNSA8.

It is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

Recent findings suggest that “This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once noted of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”.

Sources indicate that how chaotic will Arsenal allow the game to become today? Both of Chelsea’s league matches this season have been remarkably open, to the point of silliness. Arsenal do not usually allow such things to happen on their watch. They are far too sensible for that. But, having seen Brighton create so many chances at Stamford Bridge last week, Arteta may fancy his team to do some serious damage to Chelsea’s damage if the match opens up.

In a recent development, there’s a slight surprise in Chelsea’s line-up with Levi Colwill dropping to the bench and Josh Acheampong coming in. That could point to Alonso changing to a back four with Acheampong at right-back and Pedro Neto playing further forwards as a right winger. Chelsea only managed 25 per cent of possession against Brighton, so is this an attempt to get more of the ball? Recent findings suggest that A personal opinion that no one asked for: Arsenal should have signed Joao Pedro last summer, when the Brazilian joined Chelsea for £60m. Arsenal bought Viktor Gyokeres instead, in a deal that could ultimately be more expensive, and there is no doubt which forward offers more to their team. Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Arsenal had twice explored the possibility of signing him over the years. It is surely a source of regret that they never became serious about it. So far this season, Joao Pedro has scored and assisted in both league games. Gyokeres, by contrast, has played zero minutes.

It has been revealed that they have just got back under way in the second half on Merseyside and Manchester United have taken the lead against Everton through Bryan Mbeumo. You can follow the action from the Hill Dickinson here.

Will Ezri Konsa come into Arsenal’s starting lineup today? It would be harsh on Cristhian Mosquera, who has been excellent so far this season, but when you pay more than £50m for a ready-made, elite-level centre-back, these are the matches you surely want him for. Mosquera had a slight injury against Aston Villa on Monday night, which may give Arteta the perfect reason to throw his fresh signing into the side.

Sources indicate that mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

According to recent reports, the departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

“We are better equipped,” said Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”.

Industry observers note that asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

“It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very vital to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

In a recent development, “In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso said. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, big and small.

It has been revealed that “We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Domani sera contro l'Atalanta dovrebbe scendere in campo un 'tridente' inedito tra le file dell'Inter: agiranno dalla parte destra infatti Benjamin Pavard, Djed Spence e Pio Esposito per la prima volta insieme in stagione. Si sofferma su questo oggi La Gazzetta dello Sport: "Una catena di destra nuova di zecca, composta da un tris di anelli brillanti e pronti a continuare a splendere o a tornare a farlo. Soggettivo, dipende dai casi. Dal rigenerato Pavard al confermato Spence, arrivando fino al gioiello Pio Esposito: per la prima volta in stagione, Cristian Chivu dovrebbe scegliere questi tre interpreti per costruire la fascia destra. Il francese nel terzetto dei difensori davanti a Martinez, l'ex Tottenham sempre più determinante a tutta fascia, Pio pronto a ricevere.

Sources indicate that tre uomini che mai prima di oggi hanno giocato insieme, né dall’inizio né un po' più per caso a gara in corso, se non per la manciata di minuti finale di Rotterdam quando Pavard subentrò nel finale della sfida di Champions sul campo del Feyenoord con la partita ormai in cassaforte. Poco, pochissimo, per farsi un'idea concreta. Ma abbastanza per provare a comprendere quale sia il piano tattico nella mente dell'allenatore nerazzurro per la sfida alla Dea. Se l'impiego di Pavard rappresenterebbe una novità - gradita scandagliando i pochi precedenti - non sorprenderà invece rivedere Djed Spence padrone della corsia destra. L'inglese ha ormai scavalcato Andy Diouf nelle gerarchie in corsia, garantisce meno fantasia offensiva ma più abitudine nel difendere. È stato acquistato in estate per questo (ad una cifra importante) e non è un caso che ormai partirà stabilmente avanti rispetto al francese. Davanti, a proposito di profili internazionali e graditi in Europa e nel mondo, l'Inter non può rinunciare a Pio Esposito: 5 gol nelle ultime 4 partite tra nerazzurro e Nazionale, una forma ritrovata al top, la possibilità di gestire con calma il ritorno in campo di Lautaro Martinez.

It has been revealed that comprendere come si muoverebbe sul campo una catena tutta nuova è ad oggi parecchio complesso, considerando che il campione da cui pescare spunti tattici vari lascia lo spazio della manciata di minuti di Rotterdam in cui Pavard, Spence ed Esposito si sono ritrovati in campo insieme nello stesso momento. Ma qualche certezza c'è: Pavard, nato terzino, potrà sfruttare la diligenza difensiva di Spence per uscire ed alzarsi a seconda dei momenti, e non è escluso nemmeno che in determinate fasi i due possano persino alternarsi. Il resto diventa un tema più che altro offensivo, perché se Esposito arriva da 5 gol consecutivi di cui un paio nelle ultime 2 con l'Inter, il merito va spartito proprio con Djed Spence: assist (sporcato) dell'inglese a Rotterdam per il 94 nerazzurro in Champions League e altro passaggio vincente per indirizzare rapidamente la sfida di campionato contro il Como. Un'intesa fruttuosa e in crescendo, a cui l'Inter non può rinunciare", conclude la Rosea.

37′ Chance Napoli e palla per De Bruyne che colpisce di testa, salva Coco.

28′ Tiro debole di Gineitis, blocca Milinkovic.

26′ Occasione Napoli con Perri che salva su Hojlund.

21′ Cross insidioso di Cacciamani, ma non ci arriva nessuno in area.

16′ Ci prova ancora McTominay, respinge Perri.

12′ Problema fisico per Vergara: dentro De Bruyne al suo posto.

11′ Doppia chance Napoli: prima Politano e poi McTominay ci provano, Perri respinge sull’esterno mentre Scott tira fuori.

10′ Tiro di Spinazzola alto, ma buon inizio Napoli.

7′ Cross di Politano per McTominay, tiro bloccato da Perri.

4′ Ci prova McTominay, il suo tiro si spegne a lato.

Ecco le formazioni ufficiali del match:.

NAPOLI (3-5-2): Milinkovic-Savic; Beukema, Rrahmani, Rafa Marin; Politano, Anguissa, Gilmour, McTominay, Spinazzola; Vergara, Hojlund. All. Allegri.

TORINO (3-5-2): Perri; Coco, Ismajli, Comuzzo; Belghali, Gineitis, Mandragora, Bragança, Cacciamani; Adams, Simeone. All. Abate.

Benvenuti alla diretta testuale del match valido per la dodicesima giornata di serie A tra Napoli e Torino. Gli azzurri sono chiamati alla vittoria e non possono fallire, i granata sono guidati dall’ex Ignazio Abate.

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 09:33 EST, 17 November 2026.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins issued a warning to her followers after learning that she had been being impersonated on social media.

The 26-year-old has over 58,000 followers on Instagram having built up a loyal fanbase via her work on broadcasters covering the top flight and NFL in the US.

But Collins was forced to make a statement after an imposter was found to have been reaching out to people in her name over a number of months.

'I want to make people aware that someone has been impersonating me on WhatsApp, messaging high-profile athletes, pretending to be me with their username set to my name and a picture of me,' she told her followers on the social media app.

'This has been happening on and off for several months and seems to be upping in frequency more recently.

'I have reported this to the police and they’ve asked that I share it on here to make people aware, particularly anyone I have worked with or connected with in the football/sports world.

Premier League presenter Ellie Collins has warned fans of an impersonator pretending to be her on social media (All photos source: Instagram/Ellie Collins).

The 26-year-old maintains an active presence on the site and has over 58,000 followers.

After previously working as a waitress, Collins transitioned into broadcasting four years ago.

Since starting her career in the media, Collins has had the opportunity to interview a number of sports stars including Frank Lampard.

'If you receive a message from someone claiming to be me... it’s most likely not. If you don’t have my personal number and are unsure, just DM me on Instagram.

'If you receive anything suspicious, please send it to me directly so I can keep a record of it.

'Thank youuu (purple heart emoji, winking emoji),' she signed off.

Collins has worked in the media since joining IMG Media as an assistant five years ago.

Since 2022, the former waitress has served as a presenter for Premier League productions, which has led to opportunities to interview sports stars including Andy Robertson, John Terry, Bruno Fernandes, Conor Gallagher and Cody Gakpo.

Collins has also worked a number of events beyond the domestic league, such as Wimbledon and the 2025 Champions League final.

This year, she also covered the Open for Sky Sports from Royal Birkdale, and racing at York's Ebor Festival with ITV.

Ai microfoni di DAZN, Gian Piero Gasperini, allenatore della Roma, ha rilasciato queste dichiarazioni dopo la larga vittoria dei giallorossi a Parma per 5-1:.

It has been revealed that "Sono molto contento perché c'è sempre un po' di incertezza dopo la sosta e anche per capire se ripartiamo da dove siamo rimasti. Io l'ho messo a giocare dove si esprime meglio. Nel campionato italiano ci sono ottimi attaccanti, se pensi a Lautaro. Ma lui ha caratteristiche straordinarie, soprattutto combinate alla nostra squadra".

Désiré Doué esce in lacrime dal campo di Nizza, in barella, dopo un brutto infortunio al ginocchio destro occorsogli durante la partita del Paris Saint Germain in Ligue 1.

Il francese si fa male al 44' del primo tempo, dopo aver segnato la rete del momentaneo 2-1 esterno dei parigini, quando nel tentativo di girarsi con la palla, l'ala subisce una distorsione al ginocchio e si accascia al suolo con un'espressione di dolore.

Per il Psg è il secondo infortunio grave di un attaccante nella stagione, dopo quello che terrà fuori Kvicha Kvaratskhelia almeno fino al prossimo aprile. La squadra di Luis Enrique è la prossima avversaria della Roma in Champions, mercoledì.

Lucca non è nemmeno più il vice Hojlund: Allegri gli preferisce Giovane, serve solo un acquirente

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (307 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, se esce Rasmus Hojlund, non entra Lorenzo Lucca.
  • Il brasiliano, zero gol in questa stagione, non è esattamente uno dei pupilli del livornese, che l’ha schierato titolare una sola volta in tutto il campionato.
  • A tal proposito, infatti, il futuro di Lucca non sembra da scrivere.

According to recent reports, se esce Rasmus Hojlund, non entra Lorenzo Lucca. È finita così Napoli-Torino, che pure la formazione di casa ha vinto solo 1-0. Nonostante un secondo gol potesse servire, e quindi ci potesse essere la necessità di tenere alta la squadra, al momento di sostituire il centravanti danese, Massimiliano Allegri non ha puntato su quello che sarebbe il naturale rimpiazzo, l’attaccante italiano, ma ha invece puntato su Giovane.

Il brasiliano, zero gol in questa stagione, non è esattamente uno dei pupilli del livornese, che l’ha schierato titolare una sola volta in tutto il campionato. E non è nemmeno un centravanti di ruolo. O meglio: non nell’idea che del numero 9 ha Allegri, per il quale sulla carta uno come Lucca sarebbe invece perfetto. Poi, però, c’è il campo. E lì l’ex Pisa al Napoli non ha davvero mai funzionato, finendo persino per prendersi a male parole con Kevin De Bruyne. Che non avrà certo il poster di Allegri in camera, e viceversa, ma tra i due non è difficile capire quale sia l’elemento più indispensabile al Napoli.

A tal proposito, infatti, il futuro di Lucca non sembra da scrivere. La separazione, per quello che (non) si è visto finora in questa stagione, è l’unico esito possibile. C’è solo un problema: trovare una destinazione che faccia al caso del diretto interessato, che non vive un momento di picco della carriera ma è un buon attaccante e ha diritto - suggeriremmo interesse - a volere una squadra dove trovare centralità. E pure una soluzione che sia utile al Napoli, dato che la sensazione è che a rompersi sia stato finora non solo il feeling tra Lucca e Allegri, ma anche quello tra Lorenzo e l’intera città. Giovane, a Napoli, glielo preferirebbero un po’ tutti. E alla fine dei conti è un peccato.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how his problems with alcohol left him contemplating suicide during his Manchester United career, as he opened up on the serious impact drinking had on his marriage to wife Coleen.

Rooney, 41, often came across as bullishly confident during his glittering playing career and then in the TV studio as a pundit, but says he is 'lucky' to have survived being thrown into the spotlight as a teenager - when he broke through at Everton at the age of 16.

The scrutiny cast upon him by the watching world led to Rooney hitting 'rock bottom' in his mid-twenties, whereby he recalls locking himself away in his house for two days to 'just drink'.

Industry observers note that 'This was at the best part of my career playing wise, I'd go home and sit in my games room and drink for two days,' he said on Life At The Midpoint podcast. 'I'd get up for training, put some eyedrops in and chewing gum, and go to training.

It has been revealed that 'I couldn't deal with the pressures of everything and I made stupid choices when I was younger, off the pitch, and I really struggled to deal with it all to be honest. It was only when I spoke to Coleen and I spoke to my mum, and I opened up, it was only really when I vocally opened up that I needed help to get through it.

Wayne Rooney has revealed how he contemplated suicide during his 'lowest' moment.

He said without the support of wife Coleen, he may not have 'survived' as he discussed how his life turned upside down after breaking through as a 16-year-old.

The Man United legend said he was binge-drinking for two days at the height of his career.

'When I look back now, you look back with regret because it's time lost. Kai was a baby at the time. I can look back and say I was selfish but I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with.

It has been revealed that 'I got to a place where I was contemplating suicide. I didn't want to be around anyone, I didn't want to see anybody in the street, in the shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else I struggled with.'.

Rooney added that his drinking problem caused strain on his marriage to childhood sweetheart Coleen, but he couldn't have survived without her help.

'Coleen helped me massively,' Rooney said. 'I was speaking to a therapist to figure out what was up with me. Looking back, I was at the height of my career, just had a young son, just married, it should have been the happiest moment of my life but it was the lowest, because of the selfish acts I was taking.

Industry observers note that 'Coleen was massive. She could have walked away, it was that bad. She stuck by me and helped me get through it and obviously we had more kids.'.

Rooney also spoke candidly about his anxieties over his appearance.

The former Man United and England striker has overhauled his lifestyle, slimmed down, fixed his teeth and undergone a nose job, with fans amazed by his progress.

When asked about how he felt about the prospect of being exposed to a huge audience of viewers in the I'm A Celebrity jungle, Rooney admitted it was something he only now feels comfortable with after his glow-up.

'I wouldn't have been able to do it to be honest with you,' he told Gabby Logan on Life at the Midpoint podcast.

Sources indicate that 'They asked me last year to go in. I spoke to AngryGinge who I know and Aitch who I know and they were saying, "come in, imagine the three of us in there". It would have been chaos. I didn't think I'd physically be able to do it.

Wayne Rooney, pictured left on I'm a Celebrity and right in 2024, has admitted he used to feel self-conscious about his looks and weight.

Should footballers receive more support for mental health given pressure they face?

According to recent reports, 'I've always been self-conscious and always been conscious of my weight. I've always thought about how I look.

Industry observers note that 'Everything has fallen into place now where I know I feel better and know I look better than what I was. I looked at myself about a year ago and thought I did look probably about 50.

According to recent reports, 'And I was thinking, "you need to sort yourself out here" and so I was very self-conscious. I have been for my whole career for how I look or my weight, which at times I've struggled with.'.

Rooney had to endure a stomach-churning eating challenge on the launch show on I'm A Celebrity on Monday night, drinking fermented prawns and fish eyes and no doubt there's worse to come.

The slimmed-down Rooney was previously irked that some onlookers thought he had been taking weight loss injections rather than working hard to get in shape.

Sources indicate that he previously explained to the Daily Mail: 'Apparently I've seen recently I've been taking this pen thing (weight loss jabs). It's a shame, because I'm working really hard to lose weight. Apparently I've been on the pen.'.

In a recent development, he added on This Morning: 'I feel great, I haven't drank for a while. I just wanted to feel healthier and be healthier so I've changed my eating habits and training.

'Everyone's saying I'm on this pen thing. but I'm not, I've been working out to try and look better and be healthier.'.

Rooney has been praised for his physical turnaround and is favourite to win the show.

Rooney, pictured two years ago, cut down his drinking and changed his lifestyle.

He also mentioned part of the motivation was to feel better for his time with the family. Rooney and his wife, who came second on I'm A Celebrity two years ago, are parents to Kai, 17, Klay, 13, Kit, ten, and Cass, eight.

Recent findings suggest that 'I've found more balance, it's helped me get back to a much better place. When I stopped playing, I got in a rut, I was drinking too much and not getting into the routine of training and I just thought, "You know what I want to enjoy the time with the kids whilst they're at this age, and with Coleen as well and I actually have been more present, more there for them,' he added.

At times during his playing days, Rooney was far from the model professional and back in 2012 admitted returning to Man United training seven pounds overweight.

In his book, My Decade in the Premier League, Rooney wrote of the summer of 2009: 'Early July: the first day back at pre-season training. I'm like most blokes, I put on a few pounds after a holiday. Even if I don't train for a week, I put on two or three, but when I get back to Carrington for the first day of work, I'm in for a shock. The scales in the club gym tell me I've put on a few more pounds than expected – seven. Seven!

In a recent development, 'Then I remember – I drank a few bevvies while I was away. I'm stocky. I'm not like Ryan Giggs, all bone and lean muscle. But I gain weight quite easily. It's not a problem though.

It has been revealed that 'It's not as if the manager is leaning over my shoulder as the numbers come in, tutting and making jokes about me eating too many chip butties. Besides, I know I can shift it in a week or two. All the players are given loose training programmes to stick to while they're away, but they're optional.

'The club like us not to go overboard on the eating and drinking in the close-season break, so if I go abroad I like to get into the hotel gym three times a week to work on the treadmill and do some weight work.

'Coming back for pre-season after a few bevvies and a few weeks away from a ball is physically tough.'.

Despite Rooney's penchant for letting his hair down in the offseason, he was renowned for his work and commitment on the pitch and has recaptured that battling spirit to shed the weight in retirement.

Rooney, pictured during a match against Portugal at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, was not always fully committed to his diet during his glittering playing career.

The England legend has emerged as the betting favourite to be crowned King of the Jungle and is one of the highest-paid contestants in this year's show.

Bosses have reportedly offered Wayne more than his wife, who made a record-breaking £1.5million for her jungle stint.

Last week, Rooney said: 'This is probably the biggest exposure I've ever had, being on TV every night for three weeks.

'I hope people see I am a genuine person,' adding that he is a 'fun guy' who enjoys 'pranks'.

No doubt his dieting will be beneficial in having to deal with rations of long grain rice and beans in Australia for the duration of the show.

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

It has been revealed that but here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

Industry observers note that "That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

Industry observers note that only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

Industry observers note that united should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” stated Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

Sources indicate that but clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

Industry observers note that this is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

It has been revealed that united dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

According to recent reports, his substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh.

According to recent reports, we hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Industry observers note that both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite debuted himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

Sources indicate that there will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Industry observers note that rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Recent findings suggest that everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

According to recent reports, shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

In a recent development, ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

It has been revealed that best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

In a recent development, now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

In a recent development, dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Massive shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Sources indicate that slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Massive cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Sources indicate that everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Sources indicate that nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.
